description:
MEASURED s461aq, A/B on one tree via PCL_OPT (task #77's bench):

    sub calc { my $a = shift; $a * 2 + 1 }
    my %h; my $s = 0;
    for my $i (1..4e6) { my $x = calc($i); $h{$x} = 1; $s = $s + $x; delete $h{$x} }

    $x BOXED (gate off): 1.5472 s exec
    $x RAW   (gate on) : 1.7002 s exec      -> the raw slot is 9.9 % SLOWER

Cause: a p-box caches its stringification (`p-box-sv`), so the second and
third hash operations on the same value reuse it; a raw number is
re-stringified at every `p-gethash`.  This is the "unboxing hash values
without also removing a lookup can be net negative" line in
faster-codegen-suggestions.md Â§Deliberately NOT worth it, now measured from
the other side â the slot, not the value.

NOT a #77 property: the PROVEN write path has always ignored USE classes
(`$x = $a + $b; $h{$x} = 1` has the same profile today), and #77 only widened
which RHS shapes are proven.  The question this files is whether the raw-slot
verdict should consult the use classes it already computes â it knows
'strkey' â and DECLINE when a numeric slot's uses are stringy.  That is a
verdict-coverage NARROWING, so its bar is the s371 one: probes + guard rows,
corpus-diff, and a bench table where no won row regresses.


ANSWERED s462as (round 19), commit ad493ac.  Direction (b) DECLINED on a
population count; direction (a) SHIPPED, and it was a TYPE, not a cache.

DIRECTION (b) — the verdict narrowing — HAS NO POPULATION.  `unboxable => 1`
from a PROVEN write ignores use classes, so the question is: how many proven
raw slots have a numeric family AND a hash-key use, where the box's cached
string form would pay for itself?  VarAnnotator was instrumented at the verdict
and run over lib/ + cpan-tests/ + perl-tests/ (~730 files, 1159 proven raw
slots):

    numeric write family                        195
    ... with >=1 stringify (str|strkey) use      16
    ... with >=1 HASH-KEY use                     0
    ... with >=2 HASH-KEY uses                    0

ZERO.  The narrowing would change no file in any population while adding a
heuristic to a proven path, and its bar (a verdict narrowing is a decline
widening, so a gate-SET scan over BOTH populations) would be paid for nothing.
The 16 stringify-use names are all num-dominant; the worst is Math::BigInt::
Calc's `$i` at num=3/str=5.  The instrument was removed, not shipped.

DIRECTION (a) SHIPPED — and the cause was not the missing cache.
`%p-fixnum-string` computed the magnitude as `(if neg (- n) n)`, whose derived
type for a FIXNUM n is `(integer 0 4611686018427387904)` — one past
most-positive-fixnum, because of most-negative-fixnum alone.  So SBCL could not
use the inline multiply-shift and EVERY `(truncate x 10)` in BOTH loops was a
full generic call, one per digit each way.  Handling that single value with the
printer lets the rest be declared.  Measured, 4e6 conversions: 7-digit 0.198 ->
0.112 s (1.8x), 2-digit 0.081 -> 0.057 s (1.4x).

A comparison-table digit count was measured and NOT taken: better on long
numbers (0.096 s) and worse on the short ones that dominate real programs
(0.066 s against 0.057 s).

A/B against 31920e0 (this session's #923 commit), interleaved, min-of-5:
  numstr (4e6 `my $s = "$i"`)   0.3237 -> 0.2971   -8.2 %
  hashkey (this task's row)     1.0854 -> 1.0298   -5.1 %
  hk4 (4 hash ops per value)    2.0211 -> 1.9273   -4.6 %
  slices                        1.1001 -> 1.0526   -4.3 %
  ovlsub -2.7 %, sliceasgn -1.2 %; arrhash (10M) / arrfill / feread / gcdrec
  flat within 0.9 %

THE GAP THIS TASK OPENED WITH, RE-MEASURED: raw vs boxed on the hash-key shape
was +10.6 % here (the task recorded 9.9 %) and is +7.4 % after the fix — a
third of it was the generic truncates, which the BOXED side paid too on its
first stringification.  The residue IS the box's SV cache, and the scaling
confirms the diagnosis: with 4 hash operations per value instead of 2 the raw
slot is +31.6 % slower, i.e. the penalty is one full stringification per
redundant hash use.  With no population to spend a verdict change on, that
residue stays.

Verified: 200 000 random values plus both fixnum limits and their neighbours
agree with WRITE-TO-STRING; the boundary list printed and used as hash keys is
byte-identical to perl 5.40.3.  Guard: Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t 123 -> 124.
subject: A raw slot can be SLOWER than a boxed one when the value is used as a hash key (the box caches its string form)
